1	# CLAUDE.md — Assignment 5 (screen-glow shader, then the crate shader)
     2	
     3	## Project context
     4	
     5	- **Engine version:** Godot 4.7 (`godot/project.godot` line 15, `config/features` lists "4.7"); the baseline log was produced by `Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official` (`logs/a3_asset_check_60fps.log` line 1).
     6	- **Renderer:** Forward+ (`godot/project.godot` line 15 lists "Forward Plus"; no `rendering_method` override in the `[rendering]` section, lines 72–74). Windows driver: D3D12 (`godot/project.godot` line 74). Physics: Jolt (`godot/project.godot` line 70).
     7	- **Main scene:** `godot/base.tscn` (`godot/project.godot` line 14 names `uid://b78l24afmav2c`, which is the uid on `godot/base.tscn` line 1). The player is instanced in it at `godot/base.tscn` line 184.
     8	- **Environment:** `WorldEnvironment` in `godot/base.tscn` lines 11–16 and 23–24 sets a background colour and ambient light only; no tonemap, exposure or glow keys are written there.
     9	
    10	### How the shaded object (the tablet screen) is drawn
    11	- Chain: `godot/base.tscn` line 184 instances `godot/characters/human/player/player.tscn`, which inherits `godot/characters/human/humanoid/humanoid.tscn` (`player.tscn` line 9); the humanoid instances `godot/items/tablet/tablet_device.tscn` as `Visual/TabletDevice` (`humanoid.tscn` lines 53–54).
    12	- The screen is the `Screen` node, a `MeshInstance3D` (`godot/items/tablet/tablet_device.tscn` lines 28–31), with a `QuadMesh` of size 0.18 × 0.108 (`tablet_device.tscn` lines 7–8) placed at z = 0.012 in front of the tablet model (`tablet_device.tscn` line 29).
    13	- Its material is `surface_material_override/0` = a `ShaderMaterial` sub-resource (`tablet_device.tscn` line 31 → lines 10–15) with `resource_local_to_scene = true` (line 11), using `res://shaders/pad_base_light.gdshader` (lines 5 and 13). Stored parameters: `cold_white = Color(0.902, 0.969, 0.969, 1)` and `pad_light_data = 0.0` (lines 14–15).

     8	## It reads no input and has no camera. A brain (PlayerController, later AI) calls apply_intent() every physics frame.
     9	
    10	# ============================================================
    11	# Constants: the three tablet states (design document section 5.8) and the two ends of the tablet move progress
    12	# ============================================================
    13	enum TabletHold {
    14		NONE,  # Not holding the tablet: the tablet is stowed on the body, switched off
    15		ONE_HAND,  # One-handed: the character holds the tablet in one hand; an operable tablet slides in at the bottom right of the screen
    16		TWO_HAND,  # Two-handed: first person, the tablet raised in front of the eyes, the character cannot move
    17	}
    18	const TABLET_MOVE_START := 0.0  # Tablet move progress: just started
    19	const TABLET_MOVE_DONE := 1.0  # Tablet move progress: arrived at the target slot
    20	const INTERACTABLE_GROUP := &"interactables"  # Everything you can press F at (now the wall light switch; later maybe doors and crates) joins this group
    21	
    22	# ============================================================
    23	# Signals: announce "what already happened", for presentation and side effects only (rule 3)
    24	# ============================================================
    25	## Emitted after the tablet state changes. Later power-on/off sounds, the slide-in animation and the raise animation listen to it.
    26	signal tablet_hold_changed(old_hold: TabletHold, new_hold: TabletHold)
    27	
    28	# ============================================================
    29	# Exported variables (@export): feel parameters shown in the Inspector and tuned there
    30	# ============================================================
    31	## Feel parameters (code rule 1a): tuned in the Inspector, not hard-coded.
    32	@export var walk_speed: float = 3.5  # Walk speed, m/s
    33	@export var sprint_speed: float = 6.0  # Sprint speed, m/s
    34	@export var turn_speed_degrees: float = 720.0  # Turn speed, degrees/s: larger = faster turning
    35	@export var acceleration: float = 42.0  # Horizontal acceleration, m/s²: the most the speed can change per second; larger = snappier starts and stops
    36	@export var jump_velocity: float = 4.5  # Upward speed at take-off, m/s
    37	@export var tablet_move_seconds: float = 0.35  # Seconds for the tablet to move from one slot to another: smaller = faster, 0 = jump there instantly
    38	
    39	# ============================================================
    40	# Member variables: state used inside this script (leading underscore = internal to this script)
    41	# ============================================================
    42	var _gravity: float = ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/3d/default_gravity")  # Gravity from the project settings (default 9.8)
    43	var _facing_yaw := 0.0  # Character facing (radians, around Y). This is "state"; Visual only displays it (rule 5)
    44	var _tablet_hold := TabletHold.NONE  # The current tablet state. Changed only through _apply_tablet_press() (rule 4)
    45	# The next few only describe "where the tablet visual has moved to": presentation, not game state (rule 5)
    46	var _tablet_shown_hold := TabletHold.NONE  # Which state's slot the tablet is moving to (or has reached)
    47	var _tablet_move_from := Transform3D.IDENTITY  # The start of this move: the tablet's position and rotation when the move began
    48	var _tablet_move_progress := TABLET_MOVE_DONE  # How far this move has gone: TABLET_MOVE_START = just started, TABLET_MOVE_DONE = arrived
    49	var _tablet_screen_lit := false #Tracks whether the screen is in the lit state
    50	
    51	# ============================================================
    52	# Node references (@onready): child nodes used in the scene
    53	# ============================================================
    54	# @onready: assigned after the node enters the scene tree and its children are ready
    55	@onready var _visual: Node3D = $Visual  # Visual node: the character model and the tablet are under it; rotating it shows the facing
    56	@onready var _human_model: Node3D = $Visual/human_model  # Character model: a capsule and a small orange box for now, a real model later
    57	@onready var _tablet: TabletDevice = $Visual/TabletDevice  # This character's own tablet (every character has one)
    58	@onready var _tablet_hip_slot: Marker3D = $Visual/TabletHipSlot  # Slot: when not held, the tablet hangs on the hip
    59	@onready var _tablet_one_hand_slot: Marker3D = $Visual/TabletOneHandSlot  # Slot: held in one hand
    60	@onready var _tablet_two_hand_slot: Marker3D = $Visual/TabletTwoHandSlot  # Slot: held in both hands, raised in front of the eyes
    61	
    62	
    63	# ============================================================
    64	# Feature functions: called by a brain, or from inside this script
    65	# ============================================================
    66	## Carries out one intent: gravity and jumping, horizontal movement along the look direction, turning (facing the look direction while aiming), collisions, then updates the visuals.
    67	## Called once per physics frame by the brain (no underscore = a public function for outside callers).
    68	## The body (CharacterBody3D) itself never rotates; the facing is only stored in _facing_yaw.
    69	func apply_intent(intent: CharacterIntent, delta: float) -> void:
    70		_apply_tablet_press(intent.tablet_press)  # Tablet key first: the turning later in this frame uses the new tablet state
    71		if intent.interact:  # If the brain says "I want to interact this frame",
    72			_try_interact()  # we look for something nearby we can interact with and ask it to do its thing (for example, switch the lights)
    73	
    74		# Gravity and jumping: accelerate down when off the floor; on the floor with jump pressed, give an upward speed
    75		if not is_on_floor():
    76			velocity.y -= _gravity * delta
    77		elif intent.jump:
    78			velocity.y = jump_velocity
    79	
    80		# Horizontal movement: turn "forward/back/left/right" into a world direction along the look direction (Godot's forward is -Z)
    81		var wish := Vector3(intent.move.x, 0.0, -intent.move.y).rotated(Vector3.UP, intent.look_yaw)
    82		# Target speed = direction × walk or sprint speed; a half-pushed stick gives half the speed
    83		var target := wish.normalized() * (sprint_speed if intent.sprint else walk_speed) * minf(wish.length(), 1.0)
    84		# The current horizontal speed approaches the target gradually (not instantly), so starts and stops have a short transition
    85		var horizontal := Vector3(velocity.x, 0.0, velocity.z).move_toward(target, acceleration * delta)
    86		velocity.x = horizontal.x
    87		velocity.z = horizontal.z
    88		if intent.aim or _tablet_hold == TabletHold.TWO_HAND:
    89			# While aiming: the body faces the look direction at once, and WASD becomes strafing and backing up
    90			# While holding the tablet in both hands: the body also faces the look direction, so the tablet in front of it sits right in front of the camera
    91			_facing_yaw = intent.look_yaw
    92		else:
    93			_update_facing(wish, delta)  # Normally: with movement input, the facing turns gradually toward the move direction
    94		move_and_slide()  # Built into CharacterBody3D: moves by velocity, slides along walls, stops on landing
    95		_update_visual(delta)  # Finally, show the new state on the visuals
    96	
    97	
    98	## Turns the character facing (_facing_yaw) smoothly toward direction at turn_speed_degrees.
    99	## When direction is zero (no movement input) it does nothing, and the character keeps its facing.
   100	func _update_facing(direction: Vector3, delta: float) -> void:
   101		if direction.is_zero_approx():
   102			return
   103		# A node turned θ around Y faces (-sin θ, 0, -cos θ); solve back for θ
   104		var target_yaw := atan2(-direction.x, -direction.z)
   105		# rotate_toward: turns at most one step each time and automatically takes the shorter way (never the long way round)
   106		_facing_yaw = rotate_toward(_facing_yaw, target_yaw, deg_to_rad(turn_speed_degrees) * delta)
   107	
   108	
   109	## Shows the state on the visuals: the facing and the tablet's position. A character model and animations will read the state here too.
   110	## Called once at the end of apply_intent() every physics frame.
   111	func _update_visual(delta: float) -> void:
   112		_visual.rotation.y = _facing_yaw
   113		_update_tablet_visual(delta)
   114	
   115	
   116	## Moves the tablet smoothly, over tablet_move_seconds, from where it was to the slot for the current tablet state (the raise / lower animation).
   117	## When the tablet state changes, the move restarts from where the tablet is "right now", so pressing Tab mid-move does not jump.
   118	## Reads _tablet_hold only and never changes it: presentation does not write state (rule 5). Called by _update_visual() every physics frame.
   119	func _update_tablet_visual(delta: float) -> void:
   120		# State changed: remember where the tablet is now as the start, and restart the progress
   121		if _tablet_shown_hold != _tablet_hold:
   122			_tablet_shown_hold = _tablet_hold
   123			_tablet_move_from = _tablet.transform
   124			_tablet_move_progress = TABLET_MOVE_START
   125		# Advance the progress toward "arrived": 1 / tablet_move_seconds per second, so it finishes in exactly tablet_move_seconds, independent of frame rate
   126		if tablet_move_seconds <= 0.0:
   127			_tablet_move_progress = TABLET_MOVE_DONE  # Set to 0 seconds: arrive at once
   128		else:
   129			_tablet_move_progress = move_toward(_tablet_move_progress, TABLET_MOVE_DONE, delta / tablet_move_seconds)
   130		# smoothstep: turns the even progress into "slow start, fast middle, slow stop", so it looks like a hand moving, not a machine
   131		var eased := smoothstep(TABLET_MOVE_START, TABLET_MOVE_DONE, _tablet_move_progress)
   132		var target := _get_tablet_slot(_tablet_shown_hold).transform
   133		# The tablet and the slots are all children of Visual, the same frame of reference, so interpolate directly between the two transforms (position and rotation together)
   134		_tablet.transform = _tablet_move_from.interpolate_with(target, eased)
   135		_update_tablet_screen()
   136	
   137	##Checks the current state (not held, one hand, two hands) and sends it to the tablet, so the tablet lights up or not
   138	##Called once every physics frame by _update_tablet_visual().
   139	##Reads _tablet_hold only, never changes it (rule 5)
   140	func _update_tablet_screen() -> void:
   141		if _tablet_hold == TabletHold.NONE:
   142			_tablet_screen_lit = false
   143		elif _tablet_move_progress == TABLET_MOVE_DONE:
   144			_tablet_screen_lit = true
   145		_tablet.set_screen_lit(_tablet_screen_lit)
   146	
   147	
   148	
   149	## Lookup: tablet state → which slot the tablet belongs in. Calculation only, changes nothing. Called by _update_tablet_visual().
   150	func _get_tablet_slot(hold: TabletHold) -> Marker3D:
   151		match hold:
   152			TabletHold.ONE_HAND:
   153				return _tablet_one_hand_slot
   154			TabletHold.TWO_HAND:
   155				return _tablet_two_hand_slot
   156			_:  # The remaining case: NONE (not holding the tablet)
   157				return _tablet_hip_slot
   158	
   159	
   160	## apply_intent() calls this when the intent's interact is true: find something nearby to interact with and ask it to do its thing.
   161	## Whether interaction is allowed is answered by that thing's own can_interact() (a query point, rule 3); what happens is decided by its own interact().
   162	## If several are nearby at once, we interact only with the nearest one, so one press of F does exactly one thing.
   163	func _try_interact() -> void:
   164		var nearest: Node3D = null  # First, we have not found anything to interact with yet
   165		var nearest_distance := INF  # The nearest distance starts at infinity, so the first one we find is always nearer
   166		for target in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group(INTERACTABLE_GROUP):  # We look at everything in the interactable group,
   167			if not target.can_interact(self):  # and if it says "you are too far away to interact with me",
   168				continue  # we skip it and look at the next one
   169			var distance := global_position.distance_to(target.global_position)  # Otherwise, we work out how far it is from the body
   170			if distance < nearest_distance:  # If it is nearer than everything found so far,
   171				nearest = target  # we remember it as "the nearest one"
   172				nearest_distance = distance  # and remember its distance, for the next ones to compare against
   173		if nearest != null:  # Finally, if we found one,
   174			nearest.interact(self)  # we ask it to do its thing; the switch receives this request and then switches the lights
   175	
   176	
   177	## Shows or hides this body's character model (only human_model is hidden, not the tablet, so the tablet in hand stays visible in first person).
   178	## Only affects the picture on the machine that calls it; not game state (rule 5).
   179	## Called by the player brain when switching to first person; in co-op, teammates' machines don't call it, so they still see you.
   180	func set_visual_visible(visible_locally: bool) -> void:
   181		_human_model.visible = visible_locally
   182	
   183	
   184	## Returns the current tablet state. The brain uses it to decide which inputs may go into the intent this frame.
   185	func get_tablet_hold() -> TabletHold:
   186		return _tablet_hold
   187	
   188	
   189	## Switches the tablet state by this frame's tablet key result, and emits tablet_hold_changed when the state changed.
   190	## Called by apply_intent() every physics frame; does nothing when press is NONE.
   191	func _apply_tablet_press(press: CharacterIntent.TabletPress) -> void:
   192		if press == CharacterIntent.TabletPress.NONE:
   193			return
   194		var old_hold := _tablet_hold
   195		_tablet_hold = _next_tablet_hold(old_hold, press)
   196		tablet_hold_changed.emit(old_hold, _tablet_hold)
   197	
   198	
   199	## Looks up the switching table (design document section 5.8): current state + short or long press → new state. Calculation only, changes nothing.
   200	func _next_tablet_hold(current: TabletHold, press: CharacterIntent.TabletPress) -> TabletHold:
   201		var is_long := press == CharacterIntent.TabletPress.LONG
   202		match current:  # match is the switch of other languages
   203			TabletHold.NONE:
   204				return TabletHold.TWO_HAND if is_long else TabletHold.ONE_HAND
   205			TabletHold.ONE_HAND:
   206				return TabletHold.TWO_HAND if is_long else TabletHold.NONE
   207			_:  # The remaining case: TWO_HAND (_ is switch's default)
   208				return TabletHold.NONE if is_long else TabletHold.ONE_HAND
